key_insight: Sensor2Sensor learns to convert unstructured, in-the-wild sensor streams (e.g., dashcam video) into the sensor modalities and viewpoints used by production AV fleets, enabling large-scale, diverse training data without needing new fleet drives.
problem_solved: Bridges the data gap between limited, proprietary AV fleet sensors and abundant but off-embodiment in-the-wild sources, addressing scarcity of diverse sensor configurations, geographic coverage, and long-tail scenarios for ADS training and validation.
method: Train a geometry- and sensor-aware neural conversion model to synthesize target AV sensor outputs from in-the-wild inputs (cross-embodiment sensor translation).
Combine self-supervised consistency, perceptual/reconstruction losses, and domain-adaptation/adversarial objectives to align appearance, viewpoint, and sensor characteristics.
Validate usefulness via downstream perception tasks (e.g., detection/segmentation) and by mixing synthesized data with fleet data for robust model training.
impact: Enables practitioners to massively expand and diversify ADS training sets using cheap, widely available footage, improving robustness to rare events and unseen environments while reducing dependence on expensive fleet collection.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing dashcam input -> conversion network -> synthesized AV sensor outputs -> downstream perception model
Before/after examples: raw dashcam frame vs. synthesized camera/lidar/radar views from AV embodiment

World map or heatmap illustrating expanded geographic/behavioral coverage after adding in-the-wild sources
paper_title: Sensor2Sensor: Cross-Embodiment Sensor Conversion for Autonomous Driving
paper_authors: Jiahao Wang, Bo Sun, Yijing Bai, Vincent Casser, Songyou Peng
